text:
maria: quick sync — i'm seeing no perf uplift when switching to fused-paged kernel for long-context chat (seq=8192, batch=1). can someone run a focused microbench and share traces? cc @aj @devon

aj: yes i can run. which exact model/config? fused-paged was tested on llama-2-13b in my local run earlier but that was for seq=2048. use the perf harness: 
```
./bench/run_microbench.sh --model llama-2-13b --kernel fused_paged --seq 8192 --batch 1 --device a100
```
also add `--kv-shard=none --prefetch=1` so we isolate scheduler effects

devon: flagged — PR  #842 contains the kernel-change. it landed with a fallback for small batches. i left a comment asking for a canary with long seqs. link: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/842

maria: thanks. aj can you also dump nvprof/nvtx and a short memstat trace? we want to see any unexpected memcpy spikes.

aj: yep will do. rough ETA 45m. running on pool `runtime-bench-5`. tagging bench-ci

bench-ci: schedule accepted on runtime-bench-5 (slot 2). estimated runtime 18m. job id: bench-2398765432-1

bench-bot: job bench-2398765432-1 started on node a100-17

aj: run complete. attaching summary below (pasted):
```
BENCH: model=llama-2-13b kernel=fused_paged seq=8192 batch=1
latency p50=310ms p95=590ms p99=1.2s
cpu/gpu memcpy spikes at token 1200 and token 4100 (nvtx ranges show small-copy loops)
kv cache growth steady, gpu mem ~44GB, no OOM
```

aj: nvprof stack (trimmed):
```
MemcpyAsync HtoD  3.2ms  (token 1200)
aten::fused_op_kernel  250ms steady
flash_attention_cuda  60ms per-step
```

devon: interesting — p50 still pretty good but p95/p99 tall. i wonder if the fused path is doing an extra memcpy for prefix handling in paged mode. PR 842 had a new prefix-copy for alignment, maybe that's the culprit.

sue: can you share the exact commit SHA you ran? i want to reproduce locally and add a delta benchmark with flash-only + fused-disabled.

aj: commit `4b7e2f9` (the canary merge). i reran with `--kernel flash` for baseline and got p50=300ms p95=420ms p99=760ms. so baseline better at tail.

maria: ok that supports a regression at tail. devon can you try a quick diff: remove the prefix-copy when `--prefetch=1` and see if that reduces memcpy spikes? if it's a safe toggle we can gate it behind a runtime flag.

devon: doing a quick compile now. i'll push a branch `no-prefix-copy-canary` and run the same bench.

bench-bot: job bench-2398765432-2 started on node a100-12

aj: while we wait, quick question: did anyone check if the scheduler is batching across concurrent requests (even for batch=1)? we had an issue where prefetch created pseudo-batching that added memcpy overhead.

ops-eng: scheduler logs show no cross-request coalescing on that run id. metadata: `coalesce=false`. i can dump the trace if helpful.

devon: compile done. running bench-2 now.

bench-ci: job bench-2398765432-2 finished. results posted.

devon: results: p50=305ms p95=430ms p99=780ms. memcpy spikes gone. looks like prefix-copy removed most tail latency.

aj: nice. can you paste the small patch? i'll run a quick unit and perf job on the canary cluster.

devon: patch (diff):
```
- if (prefetch) prefix_copy(...)
+ if (prefetch && enable_prefix_copy) prefix_copy(...)
```
pushed to branch `no-prefix-copy-canary`

maria: can we make that flag default-off for now and add an opt-in rollout? i'd rather not risk host breakage.

devon: agree. will open a PR with flag + config and a short blurb in the changelog. PR will include the bench artifacts.

aj: ran unit + smoke on canary cluster. all green. i'll queue a canary rollout next window (low traffic) and monitor p99 for 2 hours.

maria: awesome. please post any regression signals in #eng-runtime and tag me. if stable after 2h we can flip default.

aj: will do. thanks team :thumbsup:

bench-ci: artifacts uploaded: /artifacts/bench-2398765432/* (nvtx, memstat, perf.json)

sue: saving artifacts into `/bench-archives/2026/03/2398765432/`

maria: closing loop — move to PR review and schedule the canary. followups in PR comments. :eyes:
